text.brief: In 1881 Zhan Tianyou finished his degree at Yale's Sheffield Scientific School in the same year the Qing court recalled every student of its Educational Mission.
text.record: Yung Wing, Yale's first Chinese graduate, had persuaded the court to send 120 boys to New England between 1872 and 1875 ([Yale News: first Chinese student to graduate from an American university](https://news.yale.edu/2025/10/01/first-chinese-student-graduate-american-university); [Connecticut Humanities: Yung Wing's Dream, the Chinese Educational Mission](https://connecticuthistory.org/yung-wings-dream-the-chinese-educational-mission-1872-1881/)). The mission's conservative commissioner warned that the boys were becoming American, and the United States refused to admit any of them to West Point or Annapolis in 1878 ([Yung Wing, My Life in China and America (1909; Project Gutenberg)](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/54635/54635-h/54635-h.htm); [Connecticut Humanities: Yung Wing's Dream](https://connecticuthistory.org/yung-wings-dream-the-chinese-educational-mission-1872-1881/)). The court ordered the mission home in 1881, and Zhan later built the Beijing to Zhangjiakou railway without foreign engineers ([Connecticut Humanities: Yung Wing's Dream](https://connecticuthistory.org/yung-wings-dream-the-chinese-educational-mission-1872-1881/)).
text.reading: A host that fears what its students learn abroad recalls them, and a guest country that bars them from its best schools hands the host the reason. The Party's scholarship contracts still require state-funded students to come home and serve.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The United States promised Chinese students access to its schools in 1868 and closed its military academies to them a decade later.
text.fix: Hold the education promise open and state the security limits in advance, so a closed door is a published rule rather than a surprise.
